title: Continuous completion of a module-valued derivation
statement: Let $k$ be a commutative ring, $A$ a commutative $k$-algebra, $I\subseteq A$ a finitely generated ideal, $M$ an $A$-module, and $d:A\to M$ a $k$-derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Put $C=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}A/I^r$ and $N=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}M/I^rM$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with canonical maps $\iota:A\to C$, $j:M\to N$, and the componentwise $C$-action on $N$. Write $J=IC$, $Q_r=M/I^rM$, and $q_r:Q_{r+1}\to Q_r$ for reduction. For every $r\ge1$, the formula $d_r(a\bmod I^{r+1})=d(a)\bmod I^rM$ defines a $k$-derivation $d_r:A/I^{r+1}\to Q_r$, where the scalar action is through $A/I^{r+1}\to A/I^r$. The maps $\delta_r:C\to Q_r$, $\delta_r(x)=d_r(x_{r+1})$, satisfy $q_r\delta_{r+1}=\delta_r$. There is a unique continuous $k$-derivation $D:C\to N$ such that $D\iota=jd$, where continuity means that for each $r\ge1$ there is $s\ge1$ with $D(J^s)\subseteq I^rN$. Its coordinates are $(D(x))_r=\delta_r(x)$: equivalently, if $a\in A$ lifts $x\bmod J^{r+1}$, then $(D(x))_r=d(a)\bmod I^rM$. Moreover $D(J^{r+1})\subseteq I^rN$ for every $r\ge1$.

proof.text: By the derivation definition [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], repeated Leibniz gives $d(a_0a_1\cdots a_{r+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{r+1}(\prod_{j\ne i}a_j)d(a_i)$. If $a_1,\ldots,a_{r+1}\in I$, every summand lies in $I^rM$: the $i=0$ term has $r+1$ ideal factors and every other term has $r$. Elements of $I^{r+1}$ are finite sums of these products, so additivity gives $d(I^{r+1})\subseteq I^rM$ for every $r\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), proof of (1), Leibniz estimate, with the same calculation for an arbitrary target module

proof.text: Consequently $a\mapsto d(a)\bmod I^rM$ kills $I^{r+1}$ and descends to $d_r:A/I^{r+1}\to Q_r$. Two representatives differ by an element of $I^{r+1}$, so the formula is independent of the representative. Additivity, vanishing on $k$, and $d_r(\bar a\bar b)=\bar a\,d_r(\bar b)+\bar b\,d_r(\bar a)$ follow by reducing the corresponding identities for $d$; multiplication on $Q_r$ factors through $A/I^r$. This proves that $d_r$ is precisely the asserted $k$-derivation.

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), proof of (1), induced maps on successive quotients

proof.text: For $x\in C$, lift $x_{r+2}$ to $a\in A$. Compatibility of its coordinates gives $q_r\delta_{r+1}(x)=d(a)\bmod I^rM=\delta_r(x)$. Thus $D(x)=(\delta_r(x))_{r\geq1}$ is a compatible sequence and defines an element of $N$, by the explicit inverse-limit description [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] applied to the module quotients. The identities for $d_r$ give additivity and vanishing on $k$ coordinatewise. Moreover $\delta_r(xy)=x_r\delta_r(y)+y_r\delta_r(x)$, since $x_{r+1},y_{r+1}$ reduce to $x_r,y_r$. This is exactly the $r$-coordinate of $D(xy)=xD(y)+yD(x)$ for the stated componentwise action. Equality of compatible sequences is coordinatewise, so $D$ is a $k$-derivation. At $x=\iota(a)$ its coordinates are $d(a)\bmod I^rM$, hence $D\iota=jd$.

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), proof of (1), taking the limit; explicit module-valued verification of the derivation identities omitted there

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] first to the $A$-module $A$ and then to $M$. Its hypotheses hold because $I$ is finitely generated, with no finiteness assumption on $M$. For the coordinate maps $\pi_t:C\to A/I^t$ and $p_t:N\to M/I^tM$ this gives $\ker\pi_t=I^tC=J^t$, $\ker p_t=I^tN$, surjectivity of both maps, and $\bigcap_t I^tN=0$. The equality $I^tC=(IC)^t$ follows by expanding finite sums of products on both sides. In particular, choosing a representative $a\in A$ of $x_t$ gives $x-\iota(a)\in J^t$. Thus lifting modulo $J^{r+1}$ is the same as representing $x_{r+1}$, which proves the asserted equivalent coordinate formula.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), both parts, for the ring and for the module

proof.text: If $x\in J^{r+1}=\ker\pi_{r+1}$, then $\delta_r(x)=d_r(0)=0$. Hence $D(x)\in\ker p_r=I^rN$. Therefore $D(J^{r+1})\subseteq I^rN$, proving the stated bound and continuity with $s=r+1$.

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), proof of (1), shifted-coordinate construction; ideal-adic bound using the preceding kernel identifications

proof.text: Let $E:C\to N$ be any continuous $k$-derivation with $E\iota=jd$. Fix $r\geq1$ and choose $s_0\geq1$ with $E(J^{s_0})\subseteq I^rN$. Put $s=\max(s_0,r+1)$ and choose $a\in A$ representing $x_s$. Then $x-\iota(a)\in J^s$, and additivity gives $E(x)-j(d(a))\in I^rN$. The bound already proved for $D$ gives $D(x)-j(d(a))\in I^rN$ as well. Thus $E(x)-D(x)\in I^rN$ for every $r$, so the separatedness from Step 4 implies $E(x)=D(x)$. This holds for every $x$, and proves uniqueness.
